reason: Owns the lifetime of one explicit address-resolution action against a current facility source: availability, scoped attempt state, cache-event cancellation, matched completion effects, definite versus unknown failure, and explicit saved-state review. Native body and receipt validation are delegated to facility-action-writer, session-local attempt persistence to facility-action-attempt, and rendering to separate views. Geocode, resolve, and reviewed choice share the same facility action lifetime; no CRUD or other feature workflow is introduced. Captured source and actor gates remain visibly adjacent to their effects.

Owns one explicit provider-action dispatch from preflight through settlement. Its branches distinguish pre-dispatch refusal, native matched receipt, definite native refusal, and dispatched uncertainty; each branch settles the same token and its cache/UI effects. The source watcher is a separate named closure, current GET review is another operation, and native request/receipt validation is delegated. Keeping cleanup in finally beside the receipt/error paths makes it possible to review that obsolete attempts cannot clear a newer token or refresh a replacement view.

Owns the current facility address-resolution presentation: native status and boundary provenance, displayed candidate choices, the explicit resolve/retry controls, and a delegated status/review view. It has no direct API, receipt parsing, unknown-attempt storage, or query invalidation. Actor/client/facility lifetime is established by its keyed wrapper and dedicated controller; the view only supplies the actual displayed candidate index and returned revision.
